texts: Artificial intelligence is intelligence demonstrated by machines, as opposed to natural intelligence displayed by animals including humans.
Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language with dynamic semantics and a focus on code readability.
Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on the development of algorithms that can learn from data.
Deep learning is part of a broader family of machine learning methods based on artificial neural networks with representation learning.
Natural language processing is a subfield of linguistics and artificial intelligence concerned with interactions between computers and human language.
The Theory of Relativity, developed by Albert Einstein, revolutionized our understanding of space, time, and gravity.
Quantum mechanics is a fundamental theory in physics that describes nature at the smallest scales of energy levels.
Thermodynamics is the branch of physics that deals with heat, work, temperature, and the statistical behavior of systems.
Electromagnetism is a branch of physics involving the study of the electromagnetic force between electrically charged particles.
Astrophysics is the branch of astronomy that employs the principles of physics to study celestial objects and phenomena.
DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants use sunlight to synthesize nutrients from carbon dioxide and water.
Evolution is change in the heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations.
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms and their physical environment.
The Renaissance was a period in European history marking the transition from the Middle Ages to modernity.
World War II was a global war that lasted from 1939 to 1945 and involved the vast majority of the world nations.
The Industrial Revolution was a period of major industrialization and innovation during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
The French Revolution was a period of far-reaching social and political upheaval in France that lasted from 1789 to 1799.
Ancient Rome was a civilization that grew from a small settlement to become one of the largest empires in the ancient world.
Shakespeare was an English playwright and poet, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language.
Classical literature refers to the literature of ancient Greece and Rome, considered foundational to Western culture.
Poetry is a form of literature that uses aesthetic and rhythmic qualities of language to evoke meanings.
The novel is a relatively long work of narrative fiction, typically written in prose form.
Drama is a mode of fictional representation through dialogue and performance in theater, film, or television.
Climate change refers to long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns, mainly caused by human activities.
The water cycle describes the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth.
Biodiversity is the variety and variability of life on Earth, essential for ecosystem health and stability.
Deforestation is the permanent removal of trees to make room for agriculture or urban development.
Renewable energy is energy from sources that are naturally replenishing but flow-limited.
Democracy is a form of government in which the people have the authority to choose their governing representatives.
Capitalism is an economic system based on private ownership of the means of production and their operation for profit.
Socialism is a political and economic theory of social organization advocating collective ownership of production.
Monarchy is a form of government in which a person holds supreme power by hereditary right.
Republic is a form of government in which power resides in elected individuals representing the citizen body.
The stock market is a collection of markets where stocks are traded between investors.
Supply and demand is an economic model of price determination in a market economy.
Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money over time.
Gross domestic product is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country.
International trade is the exchange of capital, goods, and services across international borders.
The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest and largest of the three pyramids in the Giza pyramid complex.
Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel located in the Eastern Cordillera of southern Peru.
The Colosseum is an oval amphitheatre in the centre of Rome, Italy, built of travertine limestone.
Stonehenge is a prehistoric monument consisting of a ring of standing stones in Wiltshire, England.
The Parthenon is a former temple on the Athenian Acropolis dedicated to the goddess Athena.
Classical music is art music produced in the traditions of Western culture over a long period of time.
Jazz is a music genre that originated in African-American communities characterized by swing and blue notes.
Rock music is a broad genre of popular music characterized by a strong beat and electric guitars.
Hip hop is a cultural movement developed in the 1970s characterized by four key elements including rap.
Electronic music is music that employs electronic musical instruments and electronic music technology.
Abstract art uses visual language of shape, form, color and line to create compositions independent of visual references.
Impressionism is a 19th-century art movement characterized by small, visible brushstrokes and emphasis on light.
Surrealism is a cultural movement that began in the 1920s featuring unexpected juxtapositions and non sequiturs.
Cubism is an early-20th-century avant-garde art movement that revolutionized European painting and sculpture.
Renaissance art is European art from the period 1400 to 1600 characterized by realism and classical influences.
The human brain is the central organ of the nervous system and the most complex organ in the human body.
Neurons are the fundamental units of the brain and nervous system responsible for receiving sensory input.
Memory is the faculty of the brain by which information is encoded, stored, and retrieved when needed.
Consciousness is the state or quality of awareness of internal and external existence.
Cognitive psychology is the scientific study of mental processes such as attention, perception, and reasoning.
